findings.summary: Two pages use different terms for the same thing: 'Object API' and 'pyplot and object APIs'.
findings.evidence: Page 1: "Pyplot | Object API" vs page 6: "pyplot and object APIs mixed on wrong axes"
findings.fix: Use one term consistently, e.g. 'pyplot (implicit)' and 'object API (explicit ax)'.

findings.summary: The section does not cover an outline point (missing "equivalent", "accessor").
findings.evidence: kind= selects the chart: 'line' (default), 'bar', 'barh', 'hist', 'box', 'scatter', 'area', 'pie'; df.plot.bar() is the equivalent accessor form
findings.fix: Add the point with an explanation and an example.

findings.summary: The stacked and alpha examples use a single series, so they cannot show stacking or overlay.
findings.evidence: df.plot.bar(x='city', y='sales', stacked=True) and df['age'].plot.hist(bins=20, alpha=0.5) sit under the notes "stacked=True stacks columns" and "alpha=0.5 to overlay columns".
findings.fix: Use several columns. For example df.plot.bar(x='city', y=['sales','profit'], stacked=True) and df[['age','income']].plot.hist(bins=20, alpha=0.5).

findings.summary: The text says pandas may reuse the current axes when ax= is omitted, but DataFrame.plot and Series.plot create a new figure and axes in that case.
findings.evidence: Without ax=, pandas makes a new figure or reuses the current axes
findings.fix: Say that without ax=, df.plot() and s.plot() create a new figure and axes. Add that to reuse an existing axes you must pass ax= (for example ax=plt.gca()). Change the closing note to: 'Pass ax= to put a plot where you want it; otherwise pandas creates a new figure.'

findings.summary: Code block appears before its one-line idea is stated, and a stray caption trails the code.
findings.evidence: "Without ax=, pandas makes a new figure or reuses the current axes" then the python block, then "each call targets one chosen subplot"
findings.fix: State the idea (pass ax= to target a subplot) before the code and drop or move the trailing caption.

findings.summary: The 'Two scales' bullet holds two ideas: the pandas and the matplotlib route.
findings.evidence: "Two scales: plot b with secondary_y=True on the same ax" / "Matplotlib way: ax.twinx() shares x, adds a second y-axis"
findings.fix: Split these into separate one-idea bullets, or a two-row pandas vs matplotlib table.

findings.summary: The first bullet group mixes several ideas, and the code appears with only a loose lead-in.
findings.evidence: "Several metrics give grouped (side-by-side) bars by default" and "stacked=True stacks them instead" sit beside the groupby index bullet
findings.fix: Separate 'aggregate first', 'index becomes x-axis' and 'grouped vs stacked' into distinct bullets, with a small table for grouped vs stacked.

findings.summary: Several ideas share one bullet, and the hue/style/size mapping is written as a text line instead of a table.
findings.evidence: "hue = color, style = marker, size = point size"; "Draws on matplotlib axes: ax.set_title, plt.savefig still work"
findings.fix: Show the encoding mapping as a small table. Keep each bullet to one idea.

findings.summary: The scatterplot code comes before its idea is stated, and the explanation trails it.
findings.evidence: "Wants long-form (tidy) data: data=df, columns as strings" then the code, then "one call, one color per sex"
findings.fix: Put the one-line idea first ('hue splits by category in one call'), then the code.

findings.summary: The labelling code is shown before any idea is stated, and the 'Common mistakes' line is a run-on that strings four mistakes together.
findings.evidence: Section 1 opens straight with the python block; "No plt.show() in scripts; bars from unaggregated rows; pyplot and object APIs mixed on wrong axes; savefig after show."
findings.fix: Open section 1 with a one-line idea. Turn the mistakes into a bullet list, or a mistake/fix table.

findings.summary: The cheat sheet 'Plot' row packs nine arguments into one cell, so it can't be skimmed.
findings.evidence: "df.plot(kind=, x=, y=, title=, figsize=, ax=, legend=, grid=, color=)"
findings.fix: Cut it to the 3-4 key arguments, or split it into separate rows.
